reconcile.note: Gill reads Psalm 44:23's 'sleep' as God appearing inactive during affliction, not literal slumber, which Psalm 121:4 already denies.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible lists Psalm 121:4's denial of divine sleep against Psalm 44:23's plea for God to wake up as a flat, unresolved contradiction.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (1999), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord?
sides.verseText: Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord? Arise! Don't reject us forever.

sides.snippet: he who keeps Israel Will neither slumber nor sleep.
sides.verseText: Behold, he who keeps Israel Will neither slumber nor sleep.
